correctness.rationale: Prue--Scrimshaw stable-equivalence hypotheses hold for every m>=3. The two-particle cubical cells are enumerated by exact disjoint-closure constraints; each square has a unique free edge, yielding an explicit collapse to a subdivided K_{m+1} with m pendant edges and a wedge of binom(m,2) circles. An explicit integral fundamental-cycle basis z_ij and exact square boundary relations establish the arm-permutation exterior-square action and tau=-I for pole interchange. Traces follow by signed pair orbit counting. Executable complete cell/boundary/character tests at m<=5 and selected m=6,7 corroborate. No finite-only claim is used for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Two-particle graph configuration spaces are a canonical setting in graph braid topology and topological exchange on networks. The family K_{2,m} has a large natural S_m × C2 symmetry not visible from its known ordinary homology rank or circle-wedge type. The explicit integral exterior-square lattice basis and pole-swap sign give the full group action with a uniform character identity, meaningful even where nonequivariant homology is known. This is not a routine reparametrization or a single special numerical instance.
